obj/bake-the-loaf.text: Oskar hangs his own door back on his own oven, pats it twice, and the Mountain Loaf goes in.
Oskar hears where his Mountain Loaf is baking, sits down on a sack of flour, and laughs until he has to wipe his eyes.

obj/read-the-recipe.text: Oskar pushes a bucket and a bottle into your arms without looking up from his dough. 'Spring water. Honey. The castle road. Go.'

obj/win-the-door.text: Runa lifts the door off her bench and hands it over. 'Tell him I mended the hinge as well. For nothing.'
Runa turns the horseshoe over and over. 'Under the herder's eaves. All year.' The door is yours.
'You lifted it right from under my nose,' says Runa, delighted. 'Go on, then. Thief.'
Runa makes you say it again, louder, so the street hears, and then hands down the door.

on_complete.text: Hedda hands the curtain back with the lengths pencilled on it and a new set of hooks. Hung four paces back, it clears the fire lane by a hand's width. Vidar Foss is seen measuring it twice.
Vidar Foss accepted the apology in writing, in triplicate, and sat in the front row.
Vidar Foss watched the play from the guildhall steps with his arms folded. He had been accused from a window, and nobody said sorry.
The harbour children were let off, and given a pumpkin each, and Inga said the troupe could stay for supper.
The harbour children were kept in on the night of the play, and Inga did not come down from the gallery to wave.

obj/check-the-bench.text: Whoever took the curtain went past the inn towards the cathedral. The town keeps its rules there, in the By-Law Book, the old ledger of what may stand where on the square.

obj/find-the-bylaw.text: The book falls open at by-law nine, the fire lane: four paces clear of anything that burns. The bookmark is a playbill for tonight. Somebody has pencilled 'MEASURE!' across it.

on_complete.text: The jackdaw in the castle courtyard hatched four eggs that week, and Lady Agathe named every one.
Dumpling played the tail again the next year, and the year after, and hummed through every one.
The four pumpkins went back to the lighthouse and sat on Sanna's windowsill, looking pleased, until they had to be soup.
The net-menders on the quay sing the Founder's song now while they work. Most of them think it was always a song.
Fenna's chorus sang the sea crossing in four parts, one of them from inside a barrel.
Fenna sang the sea crossing on her own, and very well, and told everyone afterwards where her chorus had been.
Elin's curtain hung four paces back from the stage, red and gold, and the fire lane stayed clear. Vidar Foss was seen clapping.
The old curtain did its best. Elin's new one turned up in Hedda's cellar the next week, measured to the inch.
The whole square shouts for it again. Lady Agathe says she will come down every year until she is a hundred, and Hedda writes it down.
The town goes home pleased, full of loaf, arguing gently about who sang loudest.
Nobody can agree how the legend ends. Does the Dragon eat the loaf? Did it ever? The town argues happily on the square until the stars come out, and all the next year.

effects.text: Hedda, alone on the stage, to nobody: 'I have crossed the cold sea— no. Too much. I have crossed the sea.'
Hedda: 'And then the Dragon comes down. If the Dragon comes down. Somebody find me a Dragon.'
Bernt, from inside the gate: 'No, Dumpling. The visitors are not for floating at.'
Bernt: 'And if they ask about the costume, you know nothing. Neither do I. That is the trouble.'
Inga, calling up the lighthouse stairs: 'Sanna! Somebody's coming! Put the kettle on!'
A voice from far above: 'I'm not here!'
Fenna, in the tavern garden: 'Haul away, haul away— no. A shanty needs four voices and I have got one.'
Fenna: 'One in a barrel, one up a ladder, one waiting to be asked. Every year.'
Elin, at her empty drying frame: 'It was HERE. Nine hundred threads to the hand, and it was HERE.'
Elin: 'Who steals a curtain? Who steals a curtain on the day of the play?'
Runa, to her anvil: 'Best door in Kelderby. Mended it myself. Not giving it back.'
Runa: 'Not unless somebody says it. Out loud. Somebody.'
Oskar, to his dough: 'Rise. Rise for me. I have no door, but you rise.'
Oskar: 'Spring water and mountain honey and an oven with a door. Two out of three is nothing.'
Across the bay, from one boat to another: 'Coming in for the play?'
'Wouldn't miss it! Who's the Dragon this year?' 'Same as always, if she comes down!'

answers.done: Thirty programmes: the Founder's blue sea, the Dragon's red mountain, the Loaf's golden oven, in that order every year.

effects.text: A board of old programmes, thirty of them, every one the same three scenes: 'I. The Founder, who came over the blue sea. II. The Dragon, red on the mountain. III. The Loaf, golden from the oven.' On the oldest someone has written in pencil: 'First time. Terrified. Roared anyway.'
